episodes.192689: A remnant southwest to northeast boundary from early morning convection combined with an approaching upper trough and associated cold front, as well as anomalous precipitable water values up to 2.00 inches and CAPE around 2000 J/kg.  Resultant thunderstorms came in two phases, first a marginally severe bow echo that crossed far southwestern central Indiana, and then torrential, training downpours from northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro into Hamilton and Madison Counties.  Impacts ranged from isolated tree damage in both Knox and Daviess Counties, and then rainfall up to 4.50 inches, which included rates up to 3.00 inches/hour, that produced flash flooding in Marion, Hamilton, and Henry Counties.  The greatest impact was significant flooding on Interstate Route 465 on the Fall Creek Bridge that caused long delays during rush hour, while other flooding occurred mainly across eastern Hamilton County.
episodes.192752: Isolated to scattered strong supercell thunderstorms pushed southeast during the late morning hours. These storms developed into a line of strong to severe thunderstorms  into the early afternoon hours producing quite a bit of wind damage in portions of north central Alabama and especially portions of northeastern Alabama. A particularly large area of damage was produced by a severe downburst that occurred in the northern branch of Lake Guntersville.
episodes.192756: Daytime heating combining with high moisture content underneath the monsoon high resulted in slow moving shower and thunderstorm activity each and every day first across the mountains ranges in the afternoon before spreading to surrounding lower elevations during the evening and early overnight hours. Some thunderstorms resulted in burn scar flash flooding on the South Fork burn scar just west of Ruidoso on June 2nd, and from the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar on August 3rd.
episodes.192757: An upper level disturbance caused fairly widespread thunderstorms to break out across northeast South Carolina and southeast North Carolina. Many approached severe criteria with respect to both wind and hail.
episodes.192768: A line of thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee late in the evening of August 1, 2024. These thunderstorms were generally non-severe by the time they arrived in the area; however, they did produce sporadic severe winds, causing some damage across Sumner and Davidson counties.
episodes.192773: An early morning thunderstorm in the Bedford County area caused minor tree damage on August 2, 2024.
episodes.192837: Northwesterly flow was present over Central Alabama with an area of low pressure over Indiana and a strong ridge centered over the southwestern United States. A residual outflow boundary present over North Alabama located to the southeast of a surface front over West Tennessee prompted convective initiation during the afternoon hours of August 2. Severe thunderstorms developed along a broken line around midday, which moved southeastward through eastern Central Alabama during the afternoon. Numerous reports of damage, mainly to trees, were received from Etowah, Calhoun, St. Clair, and Talladega counties. A second complex of storms developed west of I-65 by late afternoon, with more wind damage reports from parts of Tuscaloosa, Hale, and Jefferson counties.
episodes.192838: A handful of strong storms moved northeast through southern New England on Friday afternoon bringing scattered wind damage to Massachusetts and a microburst which caused significant damage in Connecticut.
episodes.192840: A handful of strong storms moved northeast through southern New England on Friday afternoon bringing scattered wind damage to Massachusetts and a microburst which caused significant damage in Connecticut.
episodes.192841: A strong thunderstorm caused isolated wind damage to trees, utilitie poles, and a house in Rhode Island.
episodes.193054: Scattered slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated instances of gusty winds and flash flooding.
episodes.193055: Slow moving thunderstorms over Thomasville produced heavy rainfall in a short period time, leading to flash flooding.
episodes.193063: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193064: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm and humid airmass.
episodes.193072: In the midst of an abnormally hot summer, the month of August opened up with daily showers and thunderstorm chances across West Virginia. Despite the lack of strong upper level disturbances aloft to promote widespread severe weather in the state, isolated instances of downed trees from damaging wind gusts occurred on August 1st and 2nd. Convection shifted east of the Appalachian Mountains quickly each evening, diminishing the risk for severe weather.
episodes.193899: A cluster of thunderstorms developed near the WY/NE border during the afternoon of August 2. Strong wind gusts and sub-severe hail was reported with these storms.
episodes.193958: Severe thunderstorms brought isolated strong winds to 65 mph across parts of the eastern Colorado plains. In addition to this, a storm dropped golf ball (1.75 inch) hail over Elbert County just south of Agate.
episodes.193962: A surface trough was moving eastwards across the Coastal Plain on the morning of August 2nd. Out ahead of this trough isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the coast and then tracked northeastwards across the coastal waters north of Ocracoke Inlet. A few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing damaging wind gusts to the coastal waters.
episodes.193979: A passing short-wave trough enhanced a few strong to pulse severe storms during the afternoon that formed along old outflow boundaries and sea breeze collisions across SE GA over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.194427: A decaying complex of thunderstorms moved across portions of northwestern Oklahoma during the late evening of the 2nd. Strong to marginally severe wind gusts occurred along a propagating outflow across the area.
episodes.194516: Strong thunderstorms produced flash flooding in Nogales.
episodes.195025: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours over far northern Sheridan and Cherry counties. This activity then tracked to the southeast, becoming severe. Hail up to quarter size was reported in Cherry county south of Merriman.
episodes.195307: A tropical wave crossed the islands during the beginning of August, from Thursday, August 1st, through Saturday, August 3rd, which resulted in an unstable weather pattern. This weather scenario was enhanced by local topography, sea breeze variations, and afternoon effects typically observed in Puerto Rico, resulting in flooding and strong gusty winds due to thunderstorm activity.
episodes.195362: Bands of thunderstorms produced numerous instances of gale-force winds with a few instances of storm-force winds during the late afternoon to mid evening hours. There was even at least one instance of hurricane-force wind gusts over the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.195375: Several severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts over northeastern Maryland, with at least one instance of considerable wind damage noted.
episodes.195412: A robust squall line sweeping through the I-64 corridor of Southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours on the 1st crossed into Northwestern Kentucky for mid-afternoon. Several trees were damaged in Henderson and Daviess Counties, with the storm line weakening as it moved through the Pennyrile. MLCAPE values were approximately 3000 J/kg, DCAPE around 1000 J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 30 kts. Scattered showers and storms continued through the evening and overnight as a cold front moved through during the night, with storm activity in the later convection generally remaining sub-severe aside from one cell which produced wind damage in McCracken County overnight.
episodes.195442: An upper level disturbance over Central PA fueled a large cluster of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pivoted northward into an unstable environment over the Southern Tier of NY. Locally heavy rainfall accompanied the thunderstorms, and one storm in Tioga County became severe producing damaging wind gusts that knocked down a large tree, which destroyed a chicken coop.
episodes.195479: Numerous showers and some storms developed within an unstable and moist airmass in advance of an approaching front. A couple of these storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195480: Numerous showers and some storms developed within an unstable and moist airmass in advance of an approaching front. A few of these storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts.  One slow-moving storm developed across the eastern side of the City of Danville and produced three to locally four inches of rain during a two-hour period between 3:20 pm and 5:20 PM EDT.  Rainfall rates during the storm at times exceeded four inches per hour.  Crest Unit Streamflow maxed out at over 800 cfs/mi^2, which is an indication of high potential for significant flooding.  The three-hour Average Recurrence Interval for this event was a 50 to 55-year event for MRMS FLASH data.
episodes.195506: A quick 2 inches of rain fell in a very short period of time, leading to some flooding on I-94.
episodes.195528: A surface cold front approached the region as an area of low pressure tracked into the Ohio Valley. A lee trough was also present across western North Carolina. In combination of both the surface front, as well as sea breeze thunderstorms forming an effective boundary, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the Piedmont. Additional storms formed over the Sandhills and Coastal Plain. Several trees and powerlines were reported down due to the storms moving through in the late afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.195553: A few strong to severe thunderstorms caused wind damage across portions of northeastern Mississippi.
episodes.195586: An incoming system moved into a very hot and humid airmass, resulting in some showers and thunderstorms developing. Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts, downing trees and power lines across portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.195587: An incoming system moved into a very hot and humid airmass, resulting in some showers and thunderstorms developing. Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts, downing trees and power lines across portions of Delaware.
episodes.195588: An incoming system moved into a very hot and humid airmass, resulting in some showers and thunderstorms developing. Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts, downing trees and power lines across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.195674: A surface trough was moving eastwards across the Coastal Plain on the morning of August 2nd.  Widely scattered thunderstorms developed and moved through Eastern NC during the afternoon hours.  One storm became severe and produced a severe thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.195686: A deep upper level trough was over the eastern third of the US. Its axis approached through the day. Strong to severe storms developed well west of the area and eventually formed a broken line as they approached. While shear was minimal, a well-developed cold pool allowed for continued propagation with support for strong updrafts. The broken line caused damaging wind gusts over portions of the waters as it moved through.
episodes.195687: A deep upper level trough was over the eastern third of the US. Its axis approached through the day. Strong to severe storms developed well west of the area and eventually formed a broken line as they approached. While shear was minimal, a well-developed cold pool allowed for continued propagation with support for strong updrafts. The broken line produced an isolated damaging wind gust.
episodes.195692: High levels of instability associated with strong heating, moderate levels of downdraft CAPE and outflow boundaries from previous thunderstorms led to an environment supportive of severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.195714: An upper level disturbance moved along a stationary front postioned over northern Pennsylvania during the afternoon. This fueled a large cluster of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pivoted northward into an unstable environment over the Southern Tier of NY. Locally heavy rainfall accompanied the thunderstorms which triggered urban and flash flooding in the Hornell, NY area.
episodes.195734: Hot, humid conditions were present across eastern New York on Friday, August 2, 2024. Heat index values (feels-like temperatures) reached the upper 80s to low 90s across much of the region, but mid to upper 90s were reached in eastern Ulster, Dutchess, and Washington counties, creating dangerously hot and humid conditions. ||Additionally, scattered thunderstorms, some of which reached severe strength in Dutchess County, developed across portions of the region in the afternoon and evening hours. Severe thunderstorms lead to several reports of tree damage in Dutchess County.
episodes.195781: On the morning of Thursday August the 1st, a warm front was draped across portions of the state. The airmass was warm across the state, and storms were already firing off across portions of the state, including eastern Kentucky by 7am. However, the real action would come later in the day. A cold front located across Illinois, still well away from Kentucky, produced a line of storms along it during the morning hours. This line of storms gained strength, becoming a squall line and quickly dropping southeast. It reached central Kentucky by the early evening hours, then eastern Kentucky a couple hours later. By the time it got to eastern Kentucky, the line began to lose it's form, but embedded cells still packed a punch, resulting in numerous warnings across the CWA and just as many reports of wind damage. It began to regain it's linear shape by the time it reached the far eastern portion of the state, finally exiting just between 10 and 11pm EDT.
episodes.195805: By impact standards, this was the least impactful of the four days. By 12Z Friday morning, August 2nd, the cold/stationary front to our northwest finally started to push eastward into western Kentucky. A line of storms had already developed along it and pushed well ahead of it.  By the time it reached western Kentucky. The line of storms was already moving into central Kentucky. Thankfully as it reached eastern Kentucky, it began to break apart. However, embedded stronger storms within the system still led to multiple severe thunderstorm warnings just before noon. Storms continued to pop up throughout the day ahead of the approaching cold front. These storms resulted in high rainfall rates and amounts, and ultimately led to additional flash flood warnings and another severe thunderstorm warning or two. Ultimately, given the amount of warnings, the impacts were very minimal, with only one flash flood report and one thunderstorm wind damage report for the day, both in the afternoon.
episodes.195837: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across the North Carolina mountains during the afternoon western moved east into Piedmont during the late afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195842: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.195843: A mesoscale convective system moved through the northern half of East Tennessee, bringing scattered reports of straight line thunderstorm wind damage.
episodes.195844: A buoyant environment, ahead of a cold front and an upper low, sparks several rounds of scattered thunderstorms in southwest Virginia. A few instances of damaging winds and localized flooding occurred.
episodes.195935: A buoyant environment, ahead of a cold front and an upper low, sparks several rounds of scattered thunderstorms in eastern Tennessee. A few instances of localized flooding occurred as a result.
episodes.195973: A surface boundary moved south to near Interstate 40 by early afternoon of August 1st.  This boundary moved northward to near the Canadian River Valley by early evening and became a focus for thunderstorms initially near Channing and then near Canadian.  Another cluster of thunderstorms moved eastward from northeast New Mexico and into the western Oklahoma Panhandle and far northwest Texas Panhandle during the early evening.  These two large clusters of storms produced outflow boundaries that collided over the central Texas Panhandle and this collision caused more thunderstorms to develop.  There were several severe wind gusts, mainly in the central Texas Panhandle from Borger to Pampa.  A couple of severe wind gusts occurred outside of thunderstorms in areas of showers where rain was being evaporated under the cloud deck.
episodes.196029: An upper level trough transitioning over Colorado on the 1st of August provided enough instability for there to be the development of scattered strong to severe storms over Teller/El Paso counties by late in the afternoon and through the evening, resulting in several cases of severe hail reported.
episodes.196091: At the surface, a low drifted southeastward across southern Lake Michigan to near the border of northwestern IN and southwestern Lower MI during the evening of the 1st through wee hours of the 2nd. Simultaneously, a front extended eastward from the low and remained nearly-stationary in vicinity of Lake Erie, the trailing cold front drifted southeastward to northwestern IN and southern IL, and northern OH remained within the warm and humid sector. Ahead of the cold front, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms impacted Holmes County and produced isolated straight-line convective wind damage just south-southeast of Glenmont as the storms encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE, moderate DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.196229: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with convective showers embedded in strong easterly lower tropospheric flow south of a large high pressure ridge across the western north Atlantic.  Potential Tropical Cyclone Four was drifting slowly south of Cuba.
episodes.196269: A few thunderstorms with heavy rain occurred early August. The Nixon wildfire also erupted.
episodes.196283: High moisture levels on the far northern end of a tropical disturbance (future Hurricane Debby) over eastern Cuba led to the development of afternoon thunderstorms over interior sections of South Florida.

A National Weather Service storm damage survey concluded that a downburst began over a northern branch of Lake Guntersville and surged eastward. Numerous trees were uprooted and snapped along U.S. Highway 431 starting from Cooper Hill Road to Lucas Gap Road. Numerous trees were also uprooted or snapped along Snug Harbor Road with one home under construction that had a collapse of the roof structure and most walls. The tree fall pattern fanned out with trees facing northward on the northern shore of the lake branch and eastward along the southern shore of the branch. There was also some tree damage noted on Lewis Mountain with one home under construction that had partial roof damage. Damage continued with most trees facing north-northeast along White Elephant Road to the north while fanning out eastward as the wind sloped down Lewis Mountain and crossed over U.S. Highway 431. Tree damage then became sparse with only a few snapped limbs and branches before a final damage point was identified off of State Highway 79, where an open boat house was submerged in the water due to 4x4 supports giving way to the damaging winds.

Flash flooding and debris flows on the Rio Ruidoso in the Upper Canyon area along Main Road was relayed by Emergency Management and was seen on a USGS camera. Debris piled up and clogged some culverts along Main Road in Ruidoso. Another debris flow from this same heavy rain event resulted in the closure of Gavilan Canyon Bridge near Hollywood. Overall, the debris flows stayed within the banks of the Rio Ruidoso and did not overwhelm any of the main bridges in Ruidoso. Damage cost is an estimate based on cleanup costs of the clogged culverts.
